summary: FromString and fromStringOption docs need exception guarantees and a non-redundant @return tag; fromString was outside the diff and is not acted on.

resolved_items.instruction: Add to the trait description that conversion may fail, e.g., 'A type class for converting a command line `String` into a value of type `T`; conversion may throw `IllegalArgumentException`.'

Add an `@return` tag stating the guarantee the description omits — that `None` is returned when `fromString` throws, e.g., '@return `Some(value)` if conversion succeeds, or `None` if `fromString` throws.'
Use 'converted from `s`' instead of 'parsed from `s`' for terminology consistency with the trait description.

disagreements.accuracy_position: Keep @tparam T; add exception guarantee to the trait description.
disagreements.style_position: Remove @tparam T as redundant; rewrite first sentence for clarity without mentioning the exception.
disagreements.rationale: The exception guarantee is a load-bearing fact the code supports (fromString can throw IllegalArgumentException), so it must be stated; the @tparam tag is retained because the house rule only drops tags when they add nothing, and here it names the target type.

disagreements.style_position: Add a @throws tag and a full main description to fromString.
disagreements.rationale: The fromString declaration and its 'Can throw java.lang.IllegalArgumentException' comment are pre-existing and outside the diff; reviewers were instructed to judge only the added lines, so this is out of scope for this round.

disagreements.accuracy_position: Keep @return carrying the exception-to-None guarantee; drop the leading 'Returns' to avoid redundancy.
disagreements.style_position: Add @return; revise the first sentence to active present-tense declarative.
disagreements.rationale: Both agree @return is needed; the instruction keeps the tag to carry the exception guarantee per the house rule and lets style dictate the declarative phrasing.
